Playbook.name: PAN-OS — High-Severity Threat Allowed Through the Perimeter - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: PAN-OS flagged a high/critical-severity vulnerability or spyware threat whose session action was ALLOWED or only ALERTED (not reset/dropped) - the scoped replacement for the deleted catch-all External Alerts rule. Triage question: did a real high-severity threat pass the firewall, and did the affected host show follow-on compromise?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A high-severity threat the firewall let through can mean successful exploitation or active spyware/C2 - the events that most warrant a look, without the 550k/day noise of the old rule.

Assets.AssetType: Internal and DMZ hosts behind PAN-OS

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: PAN-OS logs via Elastic Agent to logs-panw.panos-* (verified live).

Fields: panw.panos.sub_type (vulnerability/spyware/CONFIG/...), panw.panos.action (alert/allow/reset-both/drop), event.severity (numeric; lower = more severe, 5 = informational), panw.panos.threat_category, panw.panos.threat.name, panw.panos.admin, panw.panos.cmd, panw.panos.path, panw.panos.result, source.ip, destination.ip, destination.port, network.application.

Signal.Name: High-sev threat allowed
Signal.Details: sub_type vulnerability/spyware, event.severity <= 2 (high/critical), action alert or allow.

InitialAssessment.Rule: 'alert' means PAN-OS detected but forwarded; 'allow' means the policy permitted it. Direction matters: an external source hitting a DMZ host is inbound exploitation; an internal source to external may be spyware/C2 egress.

Investigation.Goal: Determine the threat's direction and severity, whether it was truly allowed vs reset, and whether the affected host shows compromise.

Step.name: Threat detail, direction and enforcement
Step.Purpose: Identify the threat, its category, action, and whether the flow is inbound exploitation or outbound spyware/C2.
Step.Query: FROM logs-panw.panos-* | WHERE panw.panos.sub_type IN ("vulnerability","spyware") AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS hits = COUNT(*), threats = VALUES(panw.panos.threat.name), categories = VALUES(panw.panos.threat_category), actions = VALUES(panw.panos.action), min_sev = MIN(event.severity), apps = VALUES(network.application) BY destination.ip | SORT hits DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: min_sev <= 2 confirms high/critical. action 'allow'/'alert' = forwarded. spyware category on an INTERNAL source.ip = a bank host may be infected and beaconing - high priority. vulnerability from external = inbound exploitation.

Step.name: Did the threatened host then behave anomalously
Step.Purpose: Post-threat outbound activity from the destination host suggests the threat succeeded.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.traffic-* | WHERE source.ip == "$dest_ip" AND fortinet.firewall.action == "accept" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS conns = COUNT(*), ext_dsts = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.ip), dcountries = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.dstcountry), dports = VALUES(destination.port) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: New external connections (esp. foreign/high-risk) from the threatened host after a high-sev allowed threat corroborate compromise. Normal traffic weakens it. Cross-source corroboration only (same host), not mere time proximity.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a high/critical spyware threat from an INTERNAL source (a bank host beaconing), or INV-02 shows the threatened host beaconing externally after an allowed exploit.
Node.Result: True Positive (Compromise / Active Threat - isolate host, IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a high/critical vulnerability exploit from an external source that was allowed/alerted against a real service.
Node.Result: True Positive (Exploitation Allowed - escalate, inspect target, set action to reset)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the threat was actually reset/dropped in most events (alert is a duplicate log line) against a non-exposed target.
Node.Result: True Positive (Attack Blocked) or Benign per exposure

Node.Condition: High-sev threat allowed but direction/target sensitivity is unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-PAN-THREAT, INV-02-PAN-FOLLOWON to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A high-severity signature on benign traffic (false signature) that did not affect the host.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the signature/threat reputation; tune if a confirmed FP.

TruePositive.Definition: A real high-severity threat the firewall allowed - inbound exploitation or internal spyware/C2.

Indicators.Item: Internal source with spyware category (infected host).

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the affected host; open IR.
Change the PAN-OS action to reset/drop for the signature; block the source.
Hunt the threat across the estate.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A security profile set to alert-only (not reset) on high-severity threats (policy gap).

SOCAction.Item: Engage the firewall team to set reset/drop on high/critical signatures.
Re-triage as TP if a threat reached a host.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Isolate the affected host if compromise indicators; block the source.
Confirm the security profile action for the signature.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Set reset/drop on the signature; inspect the host; hunt the threat across the estate.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce reset/drop on high/critical signatures; reduce perimeter exposure; keep threat prevention current.

QualityChecks.Check: Replaces External Alerts (2.66M/90d). event.severity numeric, <=2 = high/critical; verified in JCB.
Direction (internal vs external source) changes the story - spyware from internal = infected host.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Benign signature confirmed; no host impact; documented.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host isolated/cleaned; signature set to reset; source blocked; estate swept.
